label: Text 1
transcript:
Aisha's grandmother does not measure things. She measures by
look, smell, and the angle of her wooden spoon. Aisha has tried
to write down the recipe for the family rice three times. Each
time, her grandmother has read the recipe and said, very gently,
"This is wrong." When Aisha asked what was wrong, her grandmother
said, "It says one teaspoon of salt. There is no teaspoon. There
is only your hand."

label: Text 2
transcript:
Anya's grandfather makes the same dish every Sunday: rice,
chicken, a sauce with herbs the family will not name in English
because the English name does not feel right. The dish has
migrated with the family for two generations. In the village,
it was made with a chicken from the yard. In the city, it is
made with a chicken from the supermarket. The taste is mostly
the same. Sundays are the day Anya's grandfather speaks the
most. The dish, he says, is what the family is. Every other
day they argue about everything. On Sundays they argue about
the chicken.
